title: The Church That God Said Made Him Want to Vomit — Revelation 3:15–16
paragraphs: The Church That God Said Made Him Want to Vomit — Revelation 3:15–16
Some churches don’t make God yawn.
They make Him sick.
Jesus looked at Laodicea and said, “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot… because you are lukewarm… I am about to spit you out of my mouth” (Revelation 3:15–16).
That is not the language of a slightly disappointed Savior.
That is holy revulsion.

Laodicea had the appearance.
Money.
Comfort.
Reputation.
Religion without fire.

They were not burning with love.
Not broken in repentance.
Not hostile enough to admit rebellion.
Just warm enough to look alive.
Just dead enough to make peace with sin.
And that is the danger.

Cold people know they need saving.
Hot people burn for the presence of God.
But lukewarm people sit in church, sing the songs, say “I’m blessed,” and slowly rot behind polished smiles.

They think activity is intimacy.
They think success is favor.
They think comfort is blessing.
But here’s what we miss…

Jesus did not rebuke Laodicea because He hated them.
He rebuked them because He loved them.
A few verses later, the same Christ who spoke of spitting them out also said, “Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline, so be zealous and repent” (Revelation 3:19).
That is the Gospel.

Jesus does not expose lukewarm hearts to destroy sinners.
He exposes them to wake them up.
To call them out of self-deception.
To pull them back from plastic Christianity.
To cleanse what religion covered and restore what pride buried.

He stands at the door and knocks.
Not because He stopped being Lord.
But because they built a church culture where He was no longer welcome at the center.
Read that again.

A church can keep its programs…
its songs…
its crowd…
its branding…
and still leave Jesus outside.
But mercy still knocks.

If your heart has cooled, repent.
If your fire has faded, return.
If your Christianity has become performance without presence, come back to Christ.
He is not looking for polished people.
He wants surrendered ones.

The same Jesus who warns is the Jesus who saves.
The same mouth that rebukes also speaks forgiveness.
The same Lord who confronts lukewarm faith still opens His arms to the repentant.
You are not too far gone.
Burn again.
